sources.title: Terrain Tiles on AWS (Mapzen terrarium elevation tiles)
sources.license: public domain (US sources), attribution in the note
sources.note: Heights from the terrarium tiles at zoom 10 (zoom 9 north of 56 N), https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png. In the United States the tiles are built from USGS 3DEP (formerly NED), SRTM and GMTED2010 (courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey) and NOAA ETOPO1, all public domain; ArcticDEM data were created from DigitalGlobe, Inc., imagery and funded under National Science Foundation awards 1043681, 1559691 and 1542736.

sources.title: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200
sources.note: Zanaga, D., Van De Kerchove, R., Daems, D., et al. (2022). ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200. doi:10.5281/zenodo.7254221. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021) processed by the ESA WorldCover consortium. Read as overview 3 (80 m pixels) of the cloud optimized files at https://esa-worldcover.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/v200/2021/map/<tile>.

sources.title: ERA5 surface extract (data/raw/climate/era5_surface)
sources.license: Copernicus licence (CC BY 4.0 compatible); attribution required
sources.note: Wind, snow and lake ice per 0.25 degree cell; picks the cells and gives each patch its wind.

not_used: Hansen Global Forest Change tree cover 2000 (CC BY 4.0, Hansen et al. 2013, Science 342:850) was considered for canopy percent. WorldCover was chosen because its overviews give 80 m land cover in one small request per 3 degree file, it is from 2021, and it also maps water, built and permanent ice.
